userVisible: The module builds as a single versioned file with a published checksum.
A caller can discover every command and whether it reads or writes data.
Selfcheck creates and migrates a fresh database, reports its runtime and integrity, and preserves existing records.
A caller can define, list and read validated record types, add compatible versions and keep existing records on their original version.
New records start in their initial stage with validated values for all ten field kinds and valid references.
Field patches preserve omitted values, remove optional values and reject removal of required values.
Only declared moves with all required fields succeed, allowed lists missing fields, and terminal stages cannot move again.
Unique values belong to only one record of a type, including when writers run concurrently.
Retrying a request returns its original result without duplicate history, while reusing its key for another request is refused.
A caller can filter, sort and limit records with stable ordering and exact numeric comparisons.
Record history preserves every successful creation, patch and move in sequence order.
Replaying generated command histories reconstructs the same records returned by query.
Analysis commands preserve stored records and database contents and never create a missing database.
The same commands, inputs, timestamps and seeds produce the same output on independent databases.
JSON input files behave like stdin and an explicit database path selects separate storage.
The release checksum matches the asset and the copied binary runs without source files or installed dependencies.
Every command follows the common JSON envelope, exit-code, determinism, forbidden-path and read-only rules.
Anyone can read and contribute to this repository: nothing in it points at a private plan or at one person's machine.
Every model of how the software behaves passes the model checker, and every deliberately broken copy is caught breaking the rule it was written to break.
